title: safeguard-controlplane-privatelink-attachment-iam-claim-operator
author: Priya Shah
body:
Motivation: In large VPC topologies we observed intermittent PrivateLink service-attachment acceptance failures during control-plane upgrades and cross-account endpoint rotations. Those failures sometimes required manual acceptance of the Service Attachment or ad-hoc IAM role provisioning. This PR implements an operator and corresponding Terraform/Helm changes that introduce a signed IAM-claim workflow to safely rotate/accept control-plane PrivateLink attachments at scale, plus pre-provision reconciliation and rollback hooks.

What this changes (single-string description): Adds a Kubernetes controller (helm chart) and companion Terraform module wiring that: 1) pre-provisions a constrained IAM role template in the control plane account for ephemeral claim-based acceptance; 2) exposes a signed-claim API (short-lived JWT) that an installer/maintainer can use to prove intent to accept an attachment; 3) automates attachment acceptance and attaches an endpoint authorization tag for auditability; 4) mirrors private DNS records into a bounded hosted zone in the managed VPC to avoid split-brain during cutovers; 5) provides a safe rollback path that can revoke claims and deprovision ephemeral roles; 6) includes migration scripts for existing installations to opt into the claim flow without downtime.

Implementation highlights: - terraform/modules/privatelink-claim: new module that creates the IAM role, a KMS key for signed claims, and tightly-scoped resource policies (assume-role condition and principal boundaries). - charts/privatelink-claim-controller: Helm chart for the controller that watches ServiceAttachment CRs (custom resource) and performs signed claim validation, acceptance, tagging, and DNS mirror writes to Route53. - installer/hooks/pre-provision-claims: introduces a preflight step in the installer that validates cross-account trust and optionally creates a bootstrap claim secret. - upgrade/rollback helpers: scripts and hooks under tools/rotate-privatelink that perform dry-run discovery, staged acceptance (canary attachments), and coordinated rollback if DNS divergence is detected.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with unit tests and policy docs - [x] Helm chart with liveness/readiness probes and RBAC manifests - [x] Controller includes reconciliation loop, exponential backoff, metrics (claim_attempts_total, claim_accept_success), and structured logs - [x] E2E test harness simulating cross-account attachment rotation - [x] Upgrade manifest and migration plan - [x] Security review and least-privilege policy approved

Testing done: Local k3s + AWS integration tests ran in CI (simulated cross-account). E2E exercises: failed claim (bad signature), expired claim, accepted claim, concurrent claim attempts, DNS mirror reconcile under network partition. CI shows all unit + e2e lanes passing; one flaky integration job was stabilized by increasing controller backoff.

Migration plan: Existing installations will run installer preflight with --enable-privatelink-claims to create initial IAM templates and bootstrap keys. The controller will operate in read-only audit mode until a final opt-in command is run. This is a non-breaking migration.

Rollback plan: The tools/rotate-privatelink/run-rollback.sh script revokes KMS keys used to sign claims and removes ephemeral IAM roles if safe. It also runs DNS reconciliation to restore pre-rotation hosted zone entries.

Security notes: Signed claims are short-lived (60s default) and KMS-backed; the ephemeral IAM role imposes a restricted assume-role condition tied to service-attachment ARNs and source-account. All actions are logged to CloudTrail and controller emits audit events to a configurable audit sink.

Release notes: Adds a claim-based PrivateLink attachment acceptance operator and Terraform/Helm wiring to enable automated, auditable control-plane PrivateLink rotations. Opt-in via installer flag.

Related: ENG-7124 (scalable privatelink rotations), ENG-7189 (dns mirroring for controlled cutovers).

d4b8e01: implement IAM role policy and KMS key provisioning
e71f9aa: add helm chart for privatelink-claim-controller (RBAC, manifests)
f9a2c33: controller: implement claim signature verification and acceptance flow
a11bc44: route53: implement dns mirror writer and reconcile loop
b22d5f7: installer: add pre-provision hooks and opt-in flag

review_comments: Ellen Park (review): Can we scope the IAM assumeRole condition to attachment ARNs instead of account-level? Reason: reduces blast radius.
Priya Shah (author): Updated iam_policies.tf to include arn:aws:ec2:::service-attachment/* as condition and added tests that assert the condition. See commit d4b8e01.
Gregory Mills (review): Controller should surface metrics for expired claims vs invalid signatures so we can tune retries. Also add a metric for simultaneous claims on same attachment.
Priya Shah (author): Added claim_expired_total and claim_signature_invalid_total, and claim_concurrent_attaches_gauge. Updated controller test to assert metric increments.
Sukriti Rao (security): KMS key rotation policy - ensure claims signed with old keys can be validated for a small grace window. Also ensure logs do not contain raw JWTs.
Priya Shah (author): Implemented a key rotation window of 5 minutes and redacted JWTs in logs. Added docs/security/privatelink-claim-policy.md.
Ellen Park (approval): LGTM after IAM scoping and metrics updates. Approved, ready to merge.
merge_outcome: merged by Ellen Park via squash merge. Merge commit message: 'feat(privatelink): add claim-based attachment acceptance operator and installer hooks - ENG-7124'
